title: A list that works at any address
hints: Two private helpers, `get<T>(offset)` and `put<T>(offset, value)` with `std::memcpy`, make every field access a one-liner and keep you away from pointer casts.

To append, find the field that should hold the new node's offset: the header's "first" field if the list is empty, otherwise the last node's "next" field. In `values`, check every offset before reading, and stop after as many nodes as could possibly fit, so a loop in corrupt data cannot run for ever.
